source: 623 deep-groove ball bearing, ISO 15 boundary dimensions 3 x 10 x 4 mm (plan.json datasheet note); minimum corner radius 0.15 mm. Printing allowances are assumptions.
frame: bearing: axis along Z, origin at the centre of face A, face B at Z = width

housing_allowance.source: assumed FDM convention: printed housing bore = outer diameter + this for a light press; +/- 0.1, tune with a test ring

shaft_clearance.source: assumed FDM convention: smooth shaft is the bore size; printed shaft stub = bore diameter minus this for a slip fit; +/- 0.05

chamfer.source: ISO 15 minimum corner radius r_s (lead-in the housing should clear)

mount.notes: Pressed into a printed housing bore (HOUSING_BORE.diameter) at least `width` deep, seated against a shoulder or retained by a lip on one face; the shoulder must stay on the outer ring, i.e. outside bore_diameter + (outer_diameter - bore_diameter) / 4 radius clearance round the bore, so the inner ring turns free (assumed convention, not a datasheet value). The outer ring in its housing and the shaft in the bore are designed contact; nothing printed may enter bore_open except the shaft.

notes: Boundary dimensions per ISO 15: d 3, D 10, B 4. Housing allowance 0.1 and shoulder rule are FDM conventions, uncertain by about 0.1 mm per printer; print a test ring.
